body_markdown:
*Industry statistics on AI app development, with practical insights for non-technical founders and small business owners building full-stack applications*


The broader AI app development market is expanding, alongside growing interest in conversational tools that help non-technical users create software.[Valued at $40.3 billion](https://market.us/report/ai-app-development-market) in 2024 and projected to reach $221.9 billion by 2034, this broader market focuses on AI-powered application development rather than specifically measuring conversational app-building platforms.


For non-technical founders seeking to validate ideas quickly, platforms like[Floot](https://floot.com/) provide full-stack infrastructure through conversational development with Claude and ChatGPT, reducing the technical work required to turn an app idea into a functioning product with hosting, a database, and user authentication.


## **Key Takeaways**


- **Market expansion:** The broader AI app development market is projected to reach[$221.9 billion by 2034](https://market.us/report/ai-app-development-market) , up from $40.3 billion in 2024.
- **Conversational app building:** Floot's[Claude and ChatGPT connector](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) allows users to build applications through existing AI subscriptions without separate Floot AI build-credit charges.
- **Non-technical adoption:** A 2025 analysis found that[63% of v0 users](https://mercury.com/blog/vibe-coding-startups-no-code) were non-developers, suggesting growing interest in app creation beyond traditional programming roles.
- **Developer AI adoption:** Stack Overflow's 2025 survey found that[84% of respondents](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2025/) used or planned to use AI tools, up from 76% in 2024.
- **Managed infrastructure:** Floot provides managed Postgres databases, authentication, and hosting to help non-technical builders deploy working applications with saved data.


## **Understanding the AI App Builder Landscape: Key Growth Metrics**


AI app builders are part of a broader software market, but their value for non-technical founders depends on more than AI-generated code. Small business owners and operators need tools that can turn plain-language instructions into working applications with user logins, saved data, payments, and reliable hosting. Platforms such as[Floot](https://floot.com/) address these requirements by combining conversational development through Claude or ChatGPT with managed full-stack infrastructure.


### **1. Market valued at $40.3 billion in 2024**


The global AI app development market reached[$40.3 billion](https://market.us/report/ai-app-development-market) in 2024, establishing a foundation for dramatic expansion over the coming decade. This figure covers the development of AI-powered applications across industries. While it does not specifically measure conversational app builders, platforms such as Floot make building and deploying applications more accessible through natural-language instructions and managed infrastructure.


### **2. Projected to reach $221.9 billion by 2034**


Industry analysts forecast the market will grow to[$221.9 billion by 2034](https://market.us/report/ai-app-development-market) , representing a transformation in how organizations approach software development. This approximately 5.5-fold increase from 2024 to 2034 reflects the mainstreaming of AI-assisted development across industries, from small startups to Fortune 500 enterprises investing in AI-powered application infrastructure.


### **3. Growth rate of 18.60% CAGR through 2034**


The sector is expanding at an[18.60% compound annual growth rate](https://market.us/report/ai-app-development-market) from 2025 to 2034, according to the market forecast. This sustained double-digit growth rate indicates strong demand for tools that lower the barriers to software creation, particularly among non-technical founders and business users seeking to validate ideas without hiring development teams.


### **4. AI apps market growing at 38.7% CAGR**


The broader AI apps market is expanding even faster, with a[38.7% CAGR](https://www.grandviewresearch.com/industry-analysis/ai-apps-market-report) projected from 2025 to 2030, indicating accelerating adoption across industries. This forecast covers AI-powered applications, a differently defined market from AI development infrastructure. The growth rates alone do not establish whether application demand is outpacing infrastructure development.


### **5. No-code AI platform market reaching $75.14 billion by 2034**


The broader no-code AI platform market was valued at[USD 6.56 billion](https://www.fortunebusinessinsights.com/no-code-ai-platform-market-110382) in 2025 and is forecast to reach $75.14 billion by 2034, with a projected 31.13% CAGR. This category includes platforms for developing and deploying AI models and should not be equated with the market for conversational web and mobile app builders.


### **6. AI-powered website builder market projected to grow 20% in 2026**


The AI-powered website builder market is projected to grow from[$2.69 billion in 2025](https://www.precedenceresearch.com/ai-powered-website-builder-market) to $3.24 billion in 2026, indicating anticipated market expansion. This single-year growth projection reflects the rapid mainstream adoption of AI-assisted web development tools among small businesses and individual creators who previously relied on template-based builders or hired designers for online presence.


### **7. Global AI software market valued at $122 billion**


The overall AI software market was[valued at $122 billion](https://www.abiresearch.com/news-resources/chart-data/report-artificial-intelligence-market-size-global) in 2024 and is projected to reach $467 billion by 2030, growing at a 25% CAGR. This broader context positions AI app builders within a massive software category that spans machine learning platforms, natural language processing, computer vision, and intelligent automation tools across every industry vertical.


## **The Rise of Conversational App Development**


Platforms that connect to existing AI assistants like Claude and ChatGPT offer distinct advantages for builders who want to leverage their current AI subscriptions. Floot's[MCP connector](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) lets users build through Claude or ChatGPT without spending Floot AI credits on ordinary connector-based building.


### **8. 63% of v0 users in a 2025 analysis were non-developers**


An analysis of[63% non-developer users](https://mercury.com/blog/vibe-coding-startups-no-code) in v0's August 2025 usage data suggests conversational development attracts people outside software engineering. The figure comes from internal analytics for one product, with no published sample size or classification method. It indicates interest among non-developers but cannot establish the percentage across all vibe coding tools.


### **9. Gartner forecast a four-to-one citizen-developer ratio at large organizations**


Gartner forecast a[four-to-one ratio](https://www.cio.com/article/191762/citizen-developer-success-requires-strong-it-oversight.html) of citizen developers to professional developers at large organizations by 2023, as reported by CIO in 2021. This was a forecast about organizational development roles, not a measured worldwide ratio or verified 2026 headcount. It illustrates anticipated interest in low-code and no-code approaches, but does not quantify the number of people building apps today.


### **10. 84% of developers use or plan to use AI tools**


In Stack Overflow's 2025 survey,[84% of respondents](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2025/) reported using or planning to use AI tools, up from 76% in 2024. This broad reported interest among survey respondents suggests AI tools are an established part of development workflows. However, the figure combines current users with those who merely plan to use AI and should not be treated as an 84% active-use rate.


### **11. 73% of AI coding-assistant users use them daily**


Stack Overflow's 2026 Developer Survey found that[73% of coding-assistant users](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2026/ai/data/ai-freq) used AI coding assistants or coding agents daily at work. Another 20.1% reported weekly use. The finding measures usage frequency among respondents already using these tools, not all developers. It illustrates how regularly AI-supported coding appears in participating professionals' workflows, while saying nothing about code quality or successful deployment.


### **12. 32% of respondents report avoiding software purchases using AI coding tools**


McKinsey's August 2026 global AI survey found that[32% of respondents](https://www.mckinsey.com/capabilities/quantumblack/our-insights/the-state-of-ai) said their organizations had decided against purchasing at least one software product or feature because they could build the functionality internally with agentic coding tools. The finding highlights growing interest in custom software development but reflects reported purchasing decisions rather than independently verified cost savings or successful production deployments.


## **Infrastructure and Deployment: Production-Grade Statistics**


For AI-built applications to deliver business value, they require robust backend infrastructure. Cloud deployment, managed databases, and scalable hosting determine whether an AI-generated app can handle real-world usage.


### **13. Cloud-based deployment holds 60% market share**


Cloud-based deployment[accounts for 60%](https://market.us/report/ai-app-development-market) of the overall AI app development market in 2024, enabling the scalability that production applications require. This dominance reflects the technical reality that modern applications need elastic infrastructure, managed services, and global content delivery networks rather than fixed on-premises servers to handle variable user loads and international audiences.


### **14. Solutions segment holds 68% of market**


The solutions segment dominates with a[68% market share](https://market.us/report/ai-app-development-market) in 2024, indicating the prominence of AI application solutions within the broader market. This market segmentation distinguishes AI application solutions from services. It does not directly measure preferences for bundled databases, hosting, authentication, or deployment.


### **15. 81% of AI website builder market uses cloud deployment**


Cloud-based SaaS deployment held[nearly 81% market share](https://www.precedenceresearch.com/ai-powered-website-builder-market) of the AI-powered website builder market in 2025, according to Precedence Research. The figure indicates cloud deployment's market dominance in this category, but does not establish that particular technologies such as serverless functions or edge caching are universally required.


### **16. Large enterprises account for 45% of the market**


Large enterprises held[over 45% market share](https://market.us/report/ai-app-development-market) in 2024, reflecting enterprise investment in AI application development across industries. This figure reflects broader enterprise investment in AI application development. However, enterprise market share should not be interpreted as direct evidence of demand for conversational app-building tools among non-technical founders and small business owners.


For those audiences, practical capabilities such as managed hosting, databases, authentication, and simple deployment are more relevant considerations. Floot addresses these infrastructure requirements through its[managed Postgres databases](https://floot.com/docs/platform/database) , serverless backend endpoints, and CDN-backed asset delivery, enabling non-technical builders to deploy production applications without DevOps expertise.


## **Mobile App Conversion and Accessibility**


The ability to convert web applications into native mobile apps expands the reach of AI-built software. Mobile deployment capabilities determine whether builders can address the dominant computing platform.


### **17. 85% of smartphones have virtual assistant capabilities**


Currently,[85% of smartphones](https://www.nextmsc.com/report/ai-app-market-ic3464) are equipped with virtual assistant capabilities, creating an environment where AI-powered interactions are expected. This statistic concerns the availability of consumer virtual assistants. It provides background on conversational technology adoption but does not directly measure demand for AI app builders or full-stack development platforms.


### **18. 44% of users actively engage with virtual assistants**


Nearly[44% of users](https://www.nextmsc.com/report/ai-app-market-ic3464) actively engage with virtual assistants across platforms, indicating comfort with AI-mediated experiences. This finding indicates usage of consumer virtual assistants, but it should not be treated as evidence that the same users are building applications through Claude, ChatGPT, or other conversational development tools.


### **19. 71% of the global population used the internet in 2024**


According to revised ITU estimates,[5.8 billion people](https://www.itu.int/en/mediacentre/Pages/PR-2025-11-17-Facts-and-Figures.aspx) used the internet in 2024, representing 71% of the global population. This large connected audience creates opportunities for builders developing web and mobile applications for international users.


Floot's[mobile app conversion](https://floot.com/docs/mobile-apps/creating-mobile-apps-in-floot) packages web applications into installable native iOS and Android shells, with build limits based on plan tier. Free plans include 2 mobile builds per month, Pro includes 12, and Power offers unlimited builds. App store publishing requires separate Apple or Google developer accounts. Floot supports iOS and Android app builds and store-submission workflows without requiring a Mac or Xcode. Developer account requirements and final app approval remain subject to Apple and Google's respective policies.


## **Integration Ecosystem Performance**


Modern applications require connections to payment processors, analytics platforms, email services, and external APIs. The breadth of available integrations determines what builders can accomplish.


### **20. NLP segment leads with 31.5% of revenue**


Natural Language Processing applications[account for 31.5%](https://www.grandviewresearch.com/industry-analysis/ai-apps-market-report) of global AI apps revenue in 2024, highlighting the importance of conversational interfaces. This category includes applications using natural language processing. Its share of the AI apps market does not directly establish demand for conversational development platforms, which are tools used to build applications rather than a single category of AI-powered end-user software.


### **21. 88% of surveyed organizations use AI in at least one function**


According to McKinsey's 2025 survey,[88% of respondents](https://www.mckinsey.com/capabilities/quantumblack/our-insights/the-state-of-ai-2025) reported regular AI use in at least one business function. This widespread organizational adoption creates internal demand for custom applications that integrate AI capabilities into existing workflows, making platforms that can quickly build AI-powered internal tools increasingly valuable to operations, HR, finance, and other non-technical departments.


Floot's[integration ecosystem](https://floot.com/en/integrations) supports connections to payment processors like Stripe, PayPal, and Square; analytics platforms including PostHog, Google Analytics, and Amplitude; email services such as Resend and SendGrid; and automation tools like Zapier and Make.


## **User Demographics and Adoption Patterns**


Understanding who builds with AI app platforms reveals market opportunities and validates use cases across industries and skill levels.


### **22. 93% to 95% of Horizons users had no prior paid web presence**


According to Hostinger's self-reported figures,[93% to 95%](https://webhosting.today/2026/06/10/lovable-bolt-and-replit-are-generating-millions-of-projects-every-week-traditional-hosting-is-not-where-they-land/) had no prior paid web presence among Horizons users. This reported percentage suggests the product attracts people without an established paid website, but it does not independently measure how many have never built a website or whether the overall market has expanded. The figure concerns one vendor's audience rather than all conversational app builders.


### **23. 47% of AI-using or AI-planning business owners cited digital assistants**


A 2023 Forbes Advisor survey of 600 US business owners who used or planned to use AI[found 47% cited assistants](https://www.forbes.com/advisor/business/software/ai-in-business/) as an AI application. This substantial adoption of conversational AI for scheduling, customer service, and administrative tasks creates familiarity with AI-driven workflows, making business owners more comfortable deploying AI-powered features in custom applications they build for customer-facing or internal use.


## **Productivity and Development Speed**


The measurable impact of AI on development speed justifies adoption for time-sensitive projects like MVP validation and market testing.


### **24. Accenture developers produced up to 8.69% more PRs with GitHub Copilot**


A study published in 2024 examined a field experiment involving 311 Accenture developers that began in 2022 and found that access to GitHub Copilot was associated with up to[8.69% more pull requests](https://mit-genai.pubpub.org/pub/v5iixksv/release/2) , depending on the analysis specification. The researchers described the experiment as statistically underpowered, so the 8.69% result should not be presented as a guaranteed productivity improvement.


## **Regional Market Distribution**


Geographic patterns in AI app builder adoption reveal where the market is maturing and where growth opportunities remain.


### **25. North America holds 38% market share**


North America captured more than[38% of the market](https://market.us/report/ai-app-development-market) in 2024 with $15.31 billion in revenue. This concentration reflects the region's established technology infrastructure, venture capital availability, and early-adopter business culture, though the cited 2024 market share does not, by itself, establish how regional shares will change in future years.


### **26. Asia-Pacific reaching 47% by 2030**


ABI Research estimated that Asia-Pacific[accounted for 33%](https://www.abiresearch.com/news-resources/chart-data/report-artificial-intelligence-market-size-global) of AI software revenue in 2025 and forecast a 47% market share by 2030. This projected increase in Asia-Pacific's share of global AI software revenue reflects ABI Research's outlook for the region, rather than a confirmed 2030 outcome.


### **27. China will represent two-thirds of Asia-Pacific revenue**


China alone will account for[two-thirds of total](https://www.abiresearch.com/news-resources/chart-data/report-artificial-intelligence-market-size-global) AI software revenue in Asia-Pacific by 2030, reaching $149.5 billion. This forecast indicates China's substantial expected contribution to Asia-Pacific AI software revenue, but it does not establish that China will surpass the United States or become the world's largest national AI software market.


### **28. 54% of AI software investment forecast from North America in 2025**


ABI Research forecasts that[54% of total](https://www.abiresearch.com/news-resources/chart-data/report-artificial-intelligence-market-size-global) AI software investment in 2025 would come from North American companies. This was ABI Research's forecast for the regional distribution of AI software investment in 2025, not a verified measurement of venture capital, corporate research spending, or government grants across regions.


## **Trust, Quality, and Security Considerations**


As AI-generated code becomes prevalent, quality and security concerns require attention from both platforms and builders.


### **29. Only 33% of surveyed developers trust AI tool accuracy**


Developer trust in AI tool accuracy has declined to 33%,[down from 43% in 2024](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2025/ai) , highlighting the importance of review processes. This erosion of confidence, despite increasing usage, reflects growing awareness of AI hallucinations, incorrect code suggestions, and outdated framework recommendations that developers encounter in production work, creating demand for platforms that implement review workflows and validation steps.


### **30. 46% of developers distrust AI tool accuracy**


Nearly[46% of developers](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2025/ai) report distrust in AI tool accuracy, emphasizing the need for human oversight. This sizable share of skeptical survey respondents highlights the importance of checking generated output. It does not mean that every AI suggestion is inaccurate, but it supports keeping human oversight in development workflows, particularly when applications handle user data or payments.


### **31. 66% say AI answers are "almost right, but not quite"**


In Stack Overflow's 2025 survey,[66% of respondents](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2025/ai) cited AI answers that were "almost right, but not quite" as a frustration, indicating that refinement cycles remain necessary. This characterization captures the current state of AI development tools: useful for generating initial implementations and reducing boilerplate work, but requiring iterative refinement and debugging that favors conversational interfaces where users can request adjustments through natural language rather than manual code editing.


### **32. 45% of tested AI code samples failed security checks**


In Veracode's spring 2026 security update,[45% of AI code-generation](https://www.veracode.com/blog/spring-2026-genai-code-security/) tests produced insecure code across four vulnerability types: SQL injection, cross-site scripting, log injection, and insecure cryptographic algorithms. These findings underscore the need to review and test AI-generated code before production deployment. The tested models sometimes generated insecure implementations for specific coding tasks. These results warrant security testing and code review before deployment, but they should not be generalized to a 45% vulnerability rate for all production code.


Floot supports secure credential management and gives users ownership of their project code, app data, and intellectual property on every plan. Database export is available on all plans, while downloadable project ZIP files require a paid plan. Third-party credentials are entered through secure browser flows rather than pasted into AI conversations. These safeguards do not replace security testing or review of AI-generated code.


## **Enterprise and Agentic AI Trends**


The evolution toward AI agents that can complete multi-step tasks autonomously represents the next frontier for app builders.


### **33. 40% of enterprise apps will feature AI agents by the end of 2026**


Gartner[predicted 40% of applications](https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2025-08-26-gartner-predicts-40-percent-of-enterprise-apps-will-feature-task-specific-ai-agents-by-2026-up-from-less-than-5-percent-in-2025) would feature task-specific AI agents by the end of 2026, up from fewer than 5% in 2025. If realized, the forecast would represent substantial adoption growth. It remains a projection rather than an observed adoption rate or proof of productivity gains across business functions.


### **34. 23% of organizations scaling agentic AI**


In McKinsey's 2025 survey,[23% of surveyed organizations](https://www.mckinsey.com/capabilities/quantumblack/our-insights/the-state-of-ai-2025) reported scaling agentic AI in at least one business function. The finding measures reported scaling activity in at least one function. It does not establish organization-wide deployment or show that autonomous agents operate at scale across every business process.


### **35. Agentic AI could drive over $450 billion in enterprise software revenue by 2035**


Under Gartner's best-case scenario, agentic AI could drive approximately[30% of enterprise application software](https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2025-08-26-gartner-predicts-40-percent-of-enterprise-apps-will-feature-task-specific-ai-agents-by-2026-up-from-less-than-5-percent-in-2025) revenue by 2035, exceeding $450 billion. This best-case projection illustrates a potential increase in revenue associated with agentic AI, rather than establishing that autonomous agents will dominate enterprise software or operate without human oversight.


### **36. 50% of knowledge workers expected to develop AI-agent skills by 2029**


Gartner predicts that by 2029, at least[50% of knowledge workers](https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2025-08-26-gartner-predicts-40-percent-of-enterprise-apps-will-feature-task-specific-ai-agents-by-2026-up-from-less-than-5-percent-in-2025) will develop skills to work with, govern or create AI agents on demand. This democratization of AI agent creation mirrors the current citizen developer movement, with business analysts, operations managers, and domain experts creating custom AI assistants for their specific workflows rather than waiting for IT departments or software vendors to build general-purpose solutions.


### **37. Worldwide AI spending forecast at $2.7 trillion in 2026**


Gartner's September 2026 forecast projects worldwide AI spending of[$2.7 trillion in 2026](https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2026-09-16-gartner-forecasts-worldwide-ai-spending-to-grow-49-point-5-percent-in-2026) , a 49.5% year-over-year increase. The spending forecast covers AI infrastructure, software, services, agents, models, and related categories. It describes the scale of the wider AI market rather than specific revenue for no-code app builders. Gartner also forecasts growing spending on AI application development platforms, but those platforms represent only one part of the total.


## **Floot's Position in the Conversational Development Market**


The statistics above validate the shift toward conversational app development and highlight infrastructure requirements that determine whether AI-generated applications can serve real business needs.


Floot positions itself at the intersection of these trends by combining MCP-based building through[Claude and ChatGPT](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) with production-grade infrastructure that includes managed Postgres databases, serverless endpoints, authentication systems, and CDN-backed hosting.


This approach serves non-technical founders and operators who want working applications with user accounts, saved data, and managed deployment. The cited industry statistics provide market context but do not directly measure demand for Floot or its infrastructure.


The data also reveals critical gaps between AI code generation and production deployment. With 45% of tested AI code samples failing security checks and only 33% of developers trusting AI tool accuracy, platforms must provide more than raw code generation. - **Secure credential handling:** Third-party API credentials are entered through browser flows rather than pasted into AI conversations, reducing exposure risk
- **Infrastructure abstraction:** Managed databases, serverless backends, and hosting remove DevOps complexity that non-technical builders cannot manage
- **Mobile deployment:** Web-to-native app conversion with tiered build limits (2 per month on Free, 12 on Pro, unlimited on Power) extends reach beyond desktop browsers
- **Integration ecosystem:** Floot supports connections to Stripe, PayPal, SendGrid, PostHog, and other services through built-in features and external APIs, with setup required for some integrations


For founders seeking to validate MVPs or launch products quickly,[Floot's pricing structure](https://floot.com/pricing) offers a free-to-start path toward production deployment, with usage-based hosting and the ability to build through existing Claude or ChatGPT subscriptions without a second Floot AI build-credit bill for connector operations.


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **How can teams build internal tools with AI without coding?**


Non-technical business owners and team leads can use AI assistants such as Claude or ChatGPT to describe the internal tool they need, including its workflows, user roles, and data requirements. Floot connects to these assistants through MCP and provides the infrastructure needed to run the application, including Postgres databases, user authentication, hosting, and file storage. This allows teams to create working internal tools without manually configuring a backend or deployment environment.


### **What is an AI app builder, and how does it differ from traditional development?**


An AI app builder is a platform that enables users to create functional web and mobile applications through natural language conversation rather than writing code. Traditional development requires programming knowledge in languages like JavaScript, Python, or Swift, while AI app builders interpret plain English descriptions and generate the necessary code, database structures, and user interfaces automatically. A 2025 analysis of v0 usage found that 63% of its users were non-developers, although the result cannot be generalized to every AI app builder.


### **How does Floot's connector model work with Claude and ChatGPT?**


[Floot's MCP connector](https://floot.com/integrations/mcp) allows users to build applications through their existing Claude or ChatGPT conversations. The AI assistant handles code generation using the user's current subscription, while Floot provides the infrastructure for deployment, databases, and hosting. This avoids a second Floot AI build-credit bill for connector-based building, though optional AI features like image generation may use separate credits. This approach differs from platforms that require dedicated AI agent subscriptions.


### **What types of applications can be built with AI app builders?**


AI app builders support a wide range of applications including ecommerce stores, booking systems, internal business tools, portfolios, landing pages, SaaS products, mobile apps, and custom workflows. Floot features community-built applications in its showcase. Floot's managed database, authentication, hosting, and integrations support applications with functionality beyond static landing pages.


### **What security considerations apply to AI-generated applications?**


Security requires attention because 45% of tested AI-generated code samples failed security checks in Veracode's evaluation, and only 33% of surveyed developers trust AI tool accuracy. Platforms should implement secure credential handling, allow code ownership and export, and provide infrastructure-level security rather than relying solely on AI-generated code. Users should also review authentication logic, validate input handling, and test payment integrations before production deployment, particularly for applications handling sensitive customer data or financial transactions.
